examples.problem_statement:
Anne could have made a larger salary elsewhere, but such (i) _________ as ample vacation time and excellent insurance persuaded her to (ii) _________.

Blank (i): perquisites / remuneration / disincentives
Blank (ii): negotiate / abscond / abide

solution.operation: Read the pivot word "but" joining the larger-salary clause to the rest of the sentence
solution.result: Anne did not leave for the larger salary; she stayed
solution.description: Use the contrast signal "but" to fix the sentence's direction: whatever follows must explain why Anne stayed rather than chased the higher pay.

solution.operation: Predict blank (i) from its own appositive list — ample vacation time and excellent insurance — as "non-salary rewards"
solution.description: Let the examples given after "such ... as" define the blank: vacation time and insurance are benefits that come on top of salary, so write that plain-language prediction before touching the choices.

solution.operation: Match the prediction "non-salary rewards" against perquisites, remuneration, disincentives
solution.description: Pick the only choice that carries the predicted meaning: perquisites (informally "perks") are exactly non-salary rewards, so it fills blank (i).

solution.operation: Predict blank (ii) as "stay" and match it against negotiate, abscond, abide
solution.description: Since step 1 established that Anne stayed, the second blank needs a word meaning "stay"; only abide can carry that sense, so it fills blank (ii).

solution.operation: Check abide's secondary senses "tolerate" and "wait for" against the sentence
solution.result: abide still fits; it is the only candidate meaning stay
solution.description: Confirm the choice by noting that abide more commonly means tolerate or wait for, yet its "stay" sense is available and no other option offers it.

key_reminders: The word but reverses direction: it signals Anne stayed instead of taking the larger salary.
Predict each blank in your own words from the sentence's own clues before reading the answer choices.
"such ___ as X and Y" makes X and Y the definition of the blank.
common_mistakes: Choosing remuneration for blank (i) — it means payment, i.e. the salary the sentence explicitly says she gave up, not the non-salary benefits.
Reading abide only as "tolerate" and rejecting it, missing the "stay" sense the sentence needs.
Choosing abscond, which means to leave secretly — the opposite of the direction "but" establishes.

examples.problem_statement:
Geoff used $630 to buy a new guitar. This amount was 15 percent of his earnings last summer.

Quantity A: The amount of Geoff's earnings last summer not used to buy the new guitar
Quantity B: $3,570

Compare Quantity A and Quantity B.

solution.operation: State what Quantity A asks for: earnings last summer minus the 630 spent on the guitar
solution.description: Name the target before computing: Quantity A is the leftover earnings, so the unknown you must find first is total earnings last summer.

solution.operation: Translate the given percent relationship into an equation: 0.15 \times (\text{earnings last summer}) = 630
solution.description: Turn the words "this amount was 15 percent of his earnings" into an arithmetic statement, with the 630 as the part and the earnings as the whole.
Solve the equation for the whole by dividing the part by the decimal form of the percent, giving Geoff's total earnings last summer.
Subtract the guitar's cost from the total earnings to get the amount he did not spend, which is Quantity A.

solution.operation: Compare Quantity A = 3570 with Quantity B = 3570
solution.description: Set the computed value of Quantity A beside the stated Quantity B; they match, so the comparison resolves to equality.

examples.answer: Choice C: The two quantities are equal.

key_reminders: Translate "A is P percent of B" directly into the equation (P/100) \times B = A.
Find the whole by dividing the part by the decimal percent, not by multiplying.
Quantity A here is the remainder after the purchase, so the subtraction step is mandatory before comparing.
common_mistakes: Comparing the whole 4200 against 3570 and answering A, forgetting that Quantity A is earnings minus the 630 spent.
Multiplying 630 by 0.15 instead of dividing, which treats the part as the whole.
Taking 630 as 15 percent of the leftover rather than of total earnings.
